findings.reason: it changes the forensic window and the hypothesis the node must test, and if `is_local` was false via the narrowed config the fix belongs in the lane-model resolution rather than in the queue branch s33 sends the node at, so the node would return a null ("both arms queue at base") and leave the real defect in place.
findings.text: s33 asserts "the queue branch ran or should have, and what actually happened is untraced" because `is_local` holds (clive == `local_backend`, verified: `reckon.flight.resolve('reckon')` reports `local_backend: clive`, and clive is the only backend declaring a `lane_document`), but a commit that changed the review-composition path landed 39 minutes earlier and can make `is_local` false without changing any code s33 read — `74f38b880` "let a named lane's model be chosen by the picker" (2026-10-19 11:10:09 +0200) rewrites `_dispatch_composed_review`'s `resolved` through `lane_model_selection(...)` / `_config_without_lane` and passes `picker_selection`, and `is_local = backend_name == local_backend and bool(local_backend)` reads that narrowed config, so a config that no longer carries `local_backend` (or carries a lane-model name in `backend_name`) sends the allowance hold down the `raise LaneHeld(lane_allowance)` arm — which queues nothing and carries exactly the router-grant reason the peer saw; the plan then instructs its own negative-result branch to enumerate "the commits since 11:49:59", a window that starts after that commit, so a node following s33 as written cannot surface the one candidate its own hypothesis ("the code may have changed since") points at
